correctness.rationale: Conservation follows from Q1=0 and symmetry; off-diagonal signs of S_h are those of the corresponding semigroup derivatives at t=alpha h. In the balanced case the eigenvectors (1,0,-1) and (1,-2,1) give decay rates c and 3c. The center diagonal has decrement (2/alpha)x exp(-3x) with x=alpha c h, attaining its maximum 2/(3e alpha); both endpoint decrements are bounded by this and the off-diagonals are positive. In the unbalanced case, symmetry and the stationary mass 1/3 leave two exponentials. Matching the initial off-diagonal value and derivative gives the printed coefficients. For the heavier edge r>s, (2r-s)^2-d^2=3r(r-s)>0, so its derivative has a negative slow term and a positive fast term. Initially the derivative is r>0; the ratio of the positive term to the magnitude of the negative term strictly decreases to zero, giving the unique claimed crossing. Rationalizing the slow coefficient gives C=r(r-s)/(2d(2r-s+d)), hence C=(r-s)/(4s)+O_s((r-s)^2); the rate difference tends to 2s and the logarithm has the stated constant and o(1) remainder. The modewise stability bound follows from maximizing x exp(-alpha x) and does not change the entry signs.
residual_risks: The crossing is for the heavier-edge entry, not necessarily the first positivity failure of the whole matrix. Finite replay is supplementary and no floating-point sign guarantee near a crossing is claimed.

evidence: Real-axis scalar stability uses |1+z exp(alpha z)|<=1. In matrix entries, the slow and fast spectral projections can have opposite signs and the balanced center diagonal has its own sharp optimum.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Power boundedness and semigroup positivity separately do not imply nonnegativity of the derivative-based step. The path-specific sign, exact-balance rigidity and delayed onset require additional analysis.

originality.rationale: The same update and the negative-real-axis modal stability threshold are credited to the originating paper. The distinct claim is the stepwise entrywise nonnegativity classification for the symmetric path, and the heavier-edge sign crossing with exact logarithmic delay. The exact path positivity comparisons involve different matrix functions and do not imply this classification.
residual_risks: The ranked corpus results and focused literature lookup do not rule out an uncatalogued monotonicity analysis of these Markov transition entries or an earlier equivalent stabilization analysis.

value.rationale: The minimal heterogeneous reversible path gives a useful exact obstruction to interpreting a spectrally stable conservative integrator as a nonnegative transport step. The abrupt requirement of exact balance and the logarithmic delay explain why strict modal contraction and even long finite-step test ranges can hide the sign failure. The balanced sharp constant and the unbalanced explicit witness supplement, rather than rephrase, standard stability background.
residual_risks: The proof is not a classification on all graphs, for all Lawson variants, or of all-entry failure thresholds in the unbalanced case.
